where_to_look: Q3 was explicitly guided to about $575m adjusted EBITDA on 2026-07-23, so the bar is the company's own number. Look at what moved inside the quarter against that guide: US HRC spot and contract price resets (CRU / Steel Market Update / SteelBenchmarker), and the lag between spot and Cliffs' contract book
Auto demand, since Cliffs is the largest supplier of automotive steel: Detroit Three Q3 North American production and October schedules, plus any UAW or supplier disruption

Outage and volume trail: the Q2 release blamed extended maintenance outages and guided Q3 shipments up about 300k tons. Look for blast-furnace or idling notices, and WARN or local-press items on Cliffs facilities from Jul–Oct
Section 232 and tariff or trade-case decisions since July, and the status of the POSCO strategic partnership, which is a balance-sheet/capital question that could land on the call

Read the 5-day drop of -6.3% into the print against steel peers that have already reported (Nucor guided mid-September and reports around this week; Steel Dynamics reported mid-October) to find out whether the move came from the sector or from CLF alone

where_to_look: Book value is the print, and it can be estimated from outside. Track agency MBS spreads to swaps and Treasuries (current-coupon OAS) from 2026-06-30 to 2026-09-30 and into October, then apply them to the $12.90 June book and 8.1x leverage. Then check whether the about 18% fall in price since the July print is in line with spread widening or goes beyond it

Peer intra-quarter book-value updates and early prints: AGNC (usually reports around the same Monday after the close), Annaly, ARMOUR, Orchid Island and Two Harbors. Any 'book value as of' disclosure in an investor deck or 8-K from mid-October is the closest proxy

The financing trail: Q2 raised $391m (about 30m shares) through the ATM. Check 424B/prospectus supplements and the share count on the 10-Q cover for Q3 issuance, which could be accretive above book or dilutive below it, now that the price is under book

The dividend: $0.17 a month was kept for October (https://finviz.com/news/401422/dynex-capital-inc-declares-october-monthly-common-stock-dividend-of-017). Look at earnings-available-for-distribution coverage against $0.51 a quarter
